the eu economy is growing but the labor market is no longer keeping pace across the european union a structural trend is becoming increasingly visible economic growth and productivity gains continue yet labor market dynamics are becoming more uneven in many member states growth is driven primarily by efficiency gains digitalization and capitalintensive investment rather than by an expansion of employment at the firm level the logic is relatively straightforward artificial intelligence and automation simplify processes reduce repetitive tasks and increase the productivity of existing teams in a context marked by geopolitical uncertainty cost pressures and multiple ongoing transitions energy digital demographic many companies prefer to optimize their current structures instead of committing to new hiring this reflects managerial caution rather than a lack of confidence in economic prospects the challenge emerges when looking at the broader picture like the us model the european growth model has long relied on the assumption that innovation and higher productivity would over time generate more jobs and better incomes recent data suggest that this link is weakening economic growth is visible in value added and profitability but it no longer translates automatically into proportional employment growth the impact is particularly evident in entrylevel and midlevel positions these roles traditionally served as gateways into the labor market or as natural steps in career progression they are now among the first to be compressed eliminated or simply not replaced ai increasingly absorbs these tasks and the result is not a wave of mass layoffs but a steady slowdown in recruitment and a reduction in professional mobility this dynamic is also visible in central and eastern europe economies that have grown in recent years through outsourced activitiesshared service centers operational it accounting and financial supportare beginning to encounter the limits of this model these are precisely the areas where automation and ai have the strongest impact local expansions are slowing teams are being consolidated and the costbased labor advantage is gradually eroding the conclusion is uncomfortable but necessary economic growth alone is no longer a sufficient indicator of labor market health an economy can become more productive and more profitable without creating jobs at the same pace if analysis remains focused solely on gdp there is a real risk of overlooking the very changes that matter most to citizens question for discussion does this trend suggest the need for eulevel adjustmentsparticularly in labor market policies taxation or reskilling frameworksto reduce the gap between economic growth and employment outcomes references eurostat unusual happened in the world of artificial intelligence the ceo of one of the most influential ai labs on earth openly admitted that what his company helped build might be causing more trouble than to think about where these ai agents could go wrong from cybersecurity vulnerabilities to mental health impacts and beyond this is a remarkable moment because it signals a shift from cheerleading innovation to confronting its potential downsides in explaining the need for this role altman acknowledged that the ai models powering todays agent systems have grown powerful enough to find critical vulnerabilities in digital infrastructures essentially spotting weaknesses in the very systems we rely on for security thats a doubleedged sword on one hand it means ai could help defenders patch weak spots faster on the other if these capabilities are misused the consequences could be severe but its not just technical risk that altman flagged he also spoke up about how increasingly sophisticated ai can affect people psychologically from mental health concerns to overdependence on these systems for advice the human side of ai interaction is becoming harder to ignore in fact altman admitted it raising futureready kids in the age of ai conversations about artificial intelligence and the future of work have become almost unavoidable at family gatherings school events or weekend barbecues someone inevitably asks is ai going to take our kids jobs another parent responds with a casual shrug kids adapt they always do both instincts are understandable yet the truth sits somewhere in between and its far more complex than simple job loss or job creation ai is reshaping the very nature of work what roles look like which skills matter most and how quickly individuals must learn and adapt these shifts will influence our children long before they ever apply for their first job the gulp moment for many parents the rise of ai triggers a moment of genuine concern this isnt the familiar story of robots assembling cars or automating repetitive tasks ai is now capable of performing many of the thinking jobs we once considered safe precisely the roles weve encouraged our children to pursue the traditional roadmap earn good grades attend a reputable university secure a stable office job is being rewritten ai has become the tireless intern that never sleeps never complains and excels at a wide range of cognitive tasks it is competing for the same desk jobs we once viewed as the pinnacle of security preparing a child for a single fixed career path software engineer analyst accountant no longer makes sense those destinations may shift dramatically and quickly the deep breath of relief despite the disruption there is reason for optimism experts widely agree that ai will not eliminate work altogether instead it will transform existing roles and create entirely new ones many of which we cannot yet imagine the key advantage for the next generation will not be knowing more facts than ai it will be knowing how to guide it our children are not training to be passengers in an aidriven world they are preparing to be pilots directing interpreting and collaborating with intelligent systems their success will depend on distinctly human strengths to support that journey we can help them build a foundation of skills that will remain valuable no matter how technology evolves the essential skill set for the ai era 1 judgment and critical thinking in a world where ai can generate endless answers the ability to evaluate those answers becomes paramount judgment means asking 1 is this accurate 2 is this ethical 3 is this wise its the internal compass that prevents a business from accepting an aigenerated recommendation that could damage its reputation or violate its values how to nurture it encourage debates at the dinner table ask why often let children make choices yes even questionable outfit combinations and experience the outcomes emphasize reasoning over correctness 2 ai literacy ai literacy is quickly becoming as fundamental as knowing how to search the internet children dont need to become programmers but they do need to understand what ai can and cannot do how to communicate with it and when to question its output how to nurture it introduce them to ageappropriate ai tools let them ask a chatbot for story ideas then evaluate the results together turn them into the familys factchecking detective 3 communication and collaboration if ai handles the first draft of most tasks the human advantage shifts to interpretation persuasion and teamwork the ability to distill a complex aigenerated report into a clear actionable insight will be invaluable so will the ability to work well with others how to nurture it encourage participation in team sports group projects or drama clubs ask them to explain weekend plans to a grandparent praise active listening and collaborative problemsolving 4 adaptability and the ability to learn the tools children learn today may be obsolete within a decade what will endure is their capacity to learn new skills quickly and confidently how to nurture it celebrate curiosity if they cycle from dinosaurs to baking to coding in a single month thats a strength not a distraction let them experiment fail and try again 5 an entrepreneurial mindset the future of work is less about climbing a single corporate ladder and more about viewing oneself as a flexible evolving portfolio of skills entrepreneurship whether formal or informal teaches initiative creativity and problemsolving how to nurture it support their small ventures from lemonade stands to online crafts discuss local problems and brainstorm solutions together focus on initiative not income a practical guide for parents 1 reframe the classic question replace what do you want to be with what problems do you want to solve or what did you enjoy learning today 2 celebrate curiosity when they ask a big question why is the sky blue respond with enthusiasm and explore the answer together 3 prioritize realworld experience internships hobbies volunteering and parttime jobs build resilience and judgment better than worksheets ever could 4 embrace technology together instead of restricting ai tools explore them side by side discuss what seems impressive what seems flawed and what feels concerning the heart of the matter we are not preparing our children for a world without work we are preparing them for a world where the most valuable currency is being deeply unmistakably human creative empathetic ethical and wise ai will be powerful but our childrens superpowers will be the qualities no machine can replicate our role is to help them strengthen those abilities so they artificial intelligence the artificial intelligence dilemma in the face of descartes cogito a logical critique the emergence of modern artificial intelligence creates a genuine philosophical dilemma for descartes cogito one that arises from the very nature of the cogitos certainty as descartes formulated it the cogito is based on a fundamental principle i think therefore i am this certainty is indubitable because it arises directly from the selfexperience of consciousness not from external appearances or the testimony of others with the advent of artificial intelligence a dual challenge emerges 1 expanding the cogito to include ai if we accept that thinking can be defined as an analytical linguistic or inferential activity then artificial intelligence fulfills these criteria ai announced its acquisition of manus a singaporebased startup renowned for its generalpurpose autonomous ai agents valued at approximately 2 billion this deal marks one of metas largest acquisitions in recent years and its fifth aifocused purchase in 2025 alone manus which rocketed from launch in march 2025 to over 100 million in annualized revenue by years end specializes in ai systems that transcend mere conversationexecuting complex multistep tasks like market research coding data analysis and workflow automation with minimal human oversight this is not just another talent grab in the ai arms race it signals a profound shift in the trajectory of synthetic intelligencehere understood as artificially constructed systems capable of reasoning planning and acting in the real world manus represents the vanguard of agentic ai systems that do not merely generate responses but actively perform work bridging the gap between todays large language models llms and tomorrows autonomous digital workforce the strategic calculus behind the deal metas move is deftly calculated while the company has poured resources into opensource foundational models like llama it has lagged in deploying practical revenuegenerating agentic applications competitors such as openai with its o1 reasoning models and operator agents anthropic claudes tooluse capabilities and google gemini integrations have made strides in agentlike functionality but manus stood out for its endtoend execution layerprocessing trillions of tokens and spinning up millions of virtual environments to complete tasks reliably by integrating manus into meta ai and its vast ecosystem spanning billions of users on facebook instagram whatsapp and beyond meta gains an immediate boost in commercialization this acquisition allows meta to leapfrog incremental improvements embedding autonomous agents into consumer tools eg planning trips or managing schedules via messenger and enterprise offerings eg automating research for advertisers it also aligns with mark zuckerbergs aggressive 2025 capex commitmentstens of billions toward ai infrastructureensuring the compute backbone for scaling these of chinese tiesno ongoing ownership or operations in china this mirrors a broader pattern cuttingedge ai talent and ip flowing westward even as domestic chinese firms like bytedance eye similar tools and iterate autonomouslyhallmarks of what many view as the next milestone en route to artificial general intelligence agi metas ownership democratizes this capability at scale potentially flooding the market with free or lowcost agents via its platforms this could compress timelines where 20242025 saw reasoning breakthroughs 2026 may deliver widespread deployment of digital employees 2 consolidation and the winnertakesmost dynamic big techs acquisition spreemeta joining amazon microsoft and others in snapping up agent startupsconcentrates innovation while opensource efforts like llama foster broad progress proprietary agent layers manuss execution engine become moats this risks stifling startups why build independently when acquihires yield billions yet it also injects massive resources accelerating safe scalable development over fragmented experiments 3 economic and societal ripples autonomous agents promise productivity explosionshandling knowledge work that currently occupies millions of hours manuss preacquisition benchmarks eg outperforming rivals in remote labor tasks hint at displacing roles in research analysis and automation integrated into metas ad ecosystem they could supercharge personalized marketing widening economic divides if access remains uneven ethically robust oversight is imperative agents amplifying biases or errors at scale pose systemic risks 4 geopolitical realignment in ai the deal underscores us dominance in absorbing global talent chinesefounded breakthroughs manus follows patterns seen in earlier migrations end up
